title: Inversion and Emphasis / Nkyerɛase ne Nnɔmba
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛbɛka ho nhia, yɛnkyerɛ pa ara na yɛbɔ mmoa a wɔfa so ka ho nhia, sɛseɛ na yɛde 'sɛ ne' anaa 'ne ne' bɔɔ. Nanso wɔ Twiriso, nnɔmba bɛba mu sɛ yɛbɔ subject-verb nkyerɛase anaa yɛde nkyerɛase bi a wɔde ka ho nhia sɛ 'not only... but also' anaa 'so + adjective... that'. Yi bi wɔ Twi a wɔde ka ho nhia, efisɛ wɔ Twi, nkyerɛase yi mma yɛn ho nhia, gyesɛ wɔ hwɛso anaa nkyerɛase a wɔde ka ho nhia. Mmoa a ɛso wɔ hɔ no ara na ɛyɛ sɛ 'Not only he arrived late' na ɛnni sɛ 'Not only did he arrive late'.
rule: Wɔ Twiriso, nkyerɛase a yɛde bɔ subject-verb no yɛ ma yɛde ka ho nhia anaa yɛde wɔ nkyerɛase a wɔde ka ho nhia. Yi bi wɔ: 1) Afe a yɛde mmoa a wɔde ka ho nhia sɛ 'never', 'rarely', 'seldom', 'hardly', 'scarcely', 'no sooner', 'not only', 'not until', 'little', 'in no way'. Wɔ mmoa yi mu, yɛde auxiliary (do/does/did, have/has, will, etc.) bɔ subject no mu, na yɛde verb no mu wɔ infinitive a ɛnni 'to'. Kyekye: 'Never have I seen such a beautiful sunset.' 2) Sɛ yɛde 'so + adjective/adverb' ne 'such + noun' bɔ nkyerɛase no mu no, yɛde 'that' (na 'that' bi wɔ hɔ): 'So beautiful was the painting that everyone stared.' 3) Ma yɛde ka ho nhia sɛ yɛde 'not only... but also', 'only after', 'only if', etc. 4) Wɔ nkyerɛase a wɔde ka ho nhia mu no, yɛde subject ne verb bɔ 'if' mu: 'Had I known, I would have come.' 5) Sɛ yɛde 'here' ne 'there' no, na verb no yɛ intransitive, na subject no yɛ noun, na ɛnni pronoun. 6) Wɔ mmoa a wɔde ka ho nhia sɛ 'may' (formal). Nnɔmba: Wɔ Twiriso, yɛmmade nkyerɛase a yɛde bɔ subject-verb no wɔ nkyerɛase a ɛyɛ normal (sɛnea ɛyɛ wɔ Twi wɔ hwɛso anaa nkyerɛase a wɔde ka ho nhia mu), na ɛmmade yɛn ho nhia sɛ yɛde hwɛso bɔ nkyerɛase no mu. Yɛnnyae sɛ mmoa a yɛde bɔ subject-verb no sɛ yɛde mmoa a wɔde ka ho nhia no, yɛde auxiliary biara, gyesɛ sɛ verb no nni auxiliary wɔ tense a ɛyɛ simple.

common_error.wrong: Not only he has a beautiful voice, but also he sings well.
common_error.correct: Not only does he have a beautiful voice, but he also sings well.
common_error.correct_alt: Not only does he have a beautiful voice, but he also sings well.
common_error.explanation: Mmoa no ba mu efisɛ wɔ Twi, yɛbɛka sɛ 'Ɔno ara na ɔwɔ twe, na ɔno ara na ɔwɔ twe', na yɛde subject-verb nkyerɛase no. Nanso wɔ Twiriso, sɛ yɛbɔ nkyerɛase no mu sɛ 'not only', yɛde auxiliary bɔ subject no mu. Enti, yɛde auxiliary 'does' wɔ present simple, na verb no 'have' wɔ base form. Yi yɛ mmoa a ɛso wɔ hɔ efisɛ yɛde Twi nkyerɛase no. Ma yɛavo mmoa no, yɛnnyae sɛ afe a yɛde 'not only', 'never', 'rarely', etc., nkyerɛase no yɛ: auxiliary + subject + verb.

levels.label: Negative Adverbial Inversion

levels.translation: Nkyerɛase a yɛde conditional ne nkyerɛase a wɔde ka ho nhia

title: Register and Style: Formal, Informal, and Neutral / Nkyerɛntɔ ne Nnesae: Nnyinasoɔ, Nnyinasoɔ, ne Nnyinasoɔ
bridge: Wɔ Twi, nkyerɛntɔ biara rekɔ so ara na ɛbɛka 'wo' anaa 'wɔ', nanso wɔ English, nkyerɛntɔ biara rekɔ so ara na ɛbɛka nsɛm, kyerɛw kronkron, ne mmara bi a ɛyɛ den. Ɛyɛ den sɛ wɔbɛka nsɛm a ɛyɛ den paa na ɛyɛ English a ɛyɛ mma anaa ɛyɛ mma paa. Sɛ woka sɛ, 'Mɛbɔa wo sɛ wɔbɛka me sɛ...', ɛyɛ nnyinasoɔ, nanso 'Mɛbɔa wo sɛ wɔbɛka me...' ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ mma wɔ nkyerɛntɔ a ɛyɛ den paa wɔ ɛbɛlabɔ a ɛyɛ den paa. Nkyerɛase ɛyɛ sɛ wɔhu mmara a ɛyɛ den paa biara na wɔnnyɛ nsɛm a ɛyɛ den paa.
rule: Wɔ English C1, nkyerɛntɔ biara rekɔ so ara na ɛbɛka nsɛm, kyerɛw kronkron, ne mmara bi a ɛyɛ den: nsɛm (e.g., 'get' vs 'obtain', 'show' vs 'demonstrate'), kyerɛw (pragmatic, passive, conditional), ne nnyinasoɔ (politeness formulas, attenuators). Nnyinasoɔ a ɛyɛ den paa rekɔ so ara na ɛbɛka nsɛm a ɛyɛ den paa, nkyerɛw a ɛyɛ den paa, ne nkyerɛw a ɛyɛ den paa ('furthermore', 'nevertheless'). Nnyinasoɔ a ɛyɛ mma rekɔ so ara na ɛbɛka nsɛm a ɛyɛ mma, mmara a ɛyɛ mma (e.g., 'put off' anaa 'postpone'), ne nsɛm a ɛyɛ mma. Nnyinasoɔ a ɛyɛ mma rekɔ so ara na ɛbɛka nsɛm a ɛyɛ mma, ɛyɛ mma, na ɛnyɛ nsɛm a ɛyɛ den paa. Sɛ woka C1, ɛsɛ sɛ wohu bɛbɛ a wɔbɛka nkyerɛntɔ biara na wɔnnyɛ nkyerɛntɔ a ɛyɛ den paa wɔ nsɛm biara.

title: Advanced Inversion and Fronting / Inversion ne Fronting akyire
bridge: Wɔ Tweneboa ne, inversion (sɛ woabɔ verb abiɛsa akyerɛ subject) ntɛm atwa mu mmom, na ɛnyɛ sɛe mmom, na ɛso wɔ hɔ ma wode akoma dan ne ma ɛda adaada biara. Wɔ Twi ne, yɛmpɛ sɛ yɛbɛka inversion no akyerɛ subject ne verb no ho asɛm, na yɛbɛka no sɛe. Sɛe, 'Rarely have I seen such beauty' a Twi ne bɛka 'Rara vez he visto tal belleza', na ɛnyɛ inversion. Nokware a ɛwɔ hɔ ne sɛ, wɔ Twi ne, inversion no wɔ sɛe a wɔde bɛka no, na wɔ Tweneboa ne, ɛwɔ affirmative sentences a wɔde bɛka no wɔ certain negative adverbs anaa restriction expressions. Hwehwɛ: mmom wɔn a wɔyɛ inversion no na wɔde bɛka no.
rule: Inversion wɔ Tweneboa ne bɛyɛ sɛ, certain elements (negative adverbs, restriction expressions, anaa frequency adverbs a wɔwɔ hɔ ma wɔde akoma dan) wɔ hɔ akyerɛ sentence no. Wɔ nhwɛso no mu, verb abiɛsa (anaa verb 'be') bɛbɔ akyerɛ subject no, sɛe structure no. Common structures no mu ne: 1) Negative adverbs: 'never', 'rarely', 'seldom', 'hardly', 'scarcely', 'barely', 'no sooner' - sɛe: 'Never have I seen such a mess'. 2) Restriction expressions: 'not only...but also', 'only after', 'only by', 'only when' - sɛe: 'Only after the war did they return'. 3) Frequency expressions with 'so' anaa 'such' - sɛe: 'So beautiful was the sunset that we stopped'. 4) With 'not until' anaa 'not since' - sɛe: 'Not until midnight did the party end'. 5) With 'in no way', 'on no account', 'under no circumstances'. Sɛ wɔnnyɛ auxiliary, de 'do/does/did' ma wɔayɛ inversion wɔ present ne past simple mu. Inversion no wɔ formal registers ne academic writing mu; wɔ everyday conversation mu, ɛnyɛ common, nanso ɛwɔ emphatic speeches mu. 'Fronting' without inversion so wɔ hɔ, sɛ wɔbɔ object anaa complement akyerɛ ma wɔde akoma dan, na subject-verb order no nni hɔ, sɛ 'That book I would never read' (na ɛnyɛ 'I would never read that book').

title: Complex Nominalization (process → processing) / Nnɔm-aboa a ɛyɛ yie (ntɛm → nnɔm-aboa a ɛyɛ yie)
bridge: Wɔ Twi, nnɔm-aboa a ɛyɛ yie wɔ mmusu ani aba nkyerɛw sɛ -m, -n, anaa -nn (sɛ nea ɛwɔ procesar → procesamiento). Nanso, wɔ English, wɔde -ing (gerund) sɛ nnɔm-aboa pii, na wɔ Twi, wɔde infinitive anaa nnɔm-aboa a ɛyɛ yie kyerɛ no. Nnɔnhwɛso a ɛyɛ yie biara ne sɛ wɔ English, gerund bi cara sɛ ɛyɛ subject, object anaa complement, nanso wɔ Twi, infinitive no ara na ɛyɛ no yie. Enti, wɔ English, wɔde nnɔm-aboa a ɛyɛ yie ne prepositions ne modifiers a wɔatwa so mmɔden (sɛ nea ɛwɔ "data processing speed"), na wɔ Twi, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔbɔ no mmɔden. Fa akwaba nso kyerɛw sɛ gerund sɛ nnɔm-aboa (the processing) ne present participle (the processing plant), efisɛ ɛmpɛ sɛ wɔbɛyɛ adwuma a ɛyɛ yie.
rule: Wɔ English, nnɔm-aboa a ɛyɛ yie de gerund (-ing) ne mmusu a wɔde -tion, -ment, -ness, -ity anaa -al ma ntɛm, adwuma anaa nneɛma a ɛyɛ yie. Gerund a ɛyɛ nnɔm-aboa wɔ nkyew biara: (1) subject: "Processing data requires time"; (2) direct object: "I enjoy processing information"; (3) preposition complement: "She is responsible for processing orders"; (4) compound modifier: "a processing plant". Wɔ nkyew a ɛyɛ yie ne akwantu (C1), wɔde nnɔm-aboa a ɛyɛ yie yi ma adwuma a ɛyɛ yie: "The processing of sensitive data is regulated" na ɛnneɛ "You must process sensitive data in a regulated way". Wɔ ntɛm a ɛyɛ yie, wɔ English pɛ gerund a ɛyɛ yie (the processing) na wɔ ntɛm a ɛyɛ yie, wɔde nnɔm-aboa a wɔde mmusu ma no (the processing, the analysis, the development). Nnɔnhwɛso: mmusu a wɔde nnɔm-aboa ma no (to decide → decision, to explain → explanation) na wɔmmu gerund a ɛyɛ nnɔm-aboa (wɔmmusɛ "the deciding" wɔ nkyew a ɛyɛ yie). Nso, wɔde nnɔm-aboa a ɛyɛ yie ma mmusu a ɛnni nhyɛso (to grow → growth, to lose → loss, to choose → choice). Wɔ compound, gerund bi cara sɛ ɛne nnɔm-aboa (processing unit) anaa nnɔm-aboa bi ne no (data processing). Sɛ wɔde gerund ne object, wɔde 'of' ma no: "the processing of data" yɛ yie wɔ nkyew bi na "data processing" yɛ yie wɔ nkyew biara. Wɔ Twi, wɔde infinitive anaa nnɔm-aboa a ɛyɛ yie kyerɛ no: "procesar datos" anaa "el procesamiento de datos".

title: Ellipsis and Substitution (so do I, neither have we) / Ɛlipsis ne Sɛnkyerɛnne
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, yɛbɛka deɛ yɛbɛka ho asɛm a ɛtɔ so ara na yɛde 'nso' ne 'entumi' ma ama yɛn kasa biara simple, nanso wɔ English mu, wɛnka ahyɛnsɛm bi anaa 'do/does/did' ma ama yɛn kasa biara. Sɛ yɛbɛka ho asɛm a ɛtɔ so ara a, ɛsɛ yɛde ahyɛnsɛm bi anaa 'do/does/did' ma ama yɛn kasa biara. Sɛ yɛbɛka ho asɛm a ɛtɔ so ara a, ɛsɛ yɛde ahyɛnsɛm bi anaa 'do/does/did' ma ama yɛn kasa biara. Sɛ yɛbɛka ho asɛm a ɛtɔ so ara a, ɛsɛ yɛde ahyɛnsɛm bi anaa 'do/does/did' ma ama yɛn kasa biara.
rule: Ɛlipsis ne Sɛnkyerɛnne wɔ English mu ma yɛn ntumi adi kan a yɛakɔe ka ho asɛm a ɛtɔ so ara. Wɔ mmerɛwa ho asɛm ne mmerɛwa a wɔka 'so' ne 'neither/nor' mu, yɛde ahyɛnsɛm a ɛyɛ ɛkwan a ɛfiri nea ɛwɔ hɔ a ɛma nea ɛwɔ hɔ no. Ahyɛnsɛm no ara na ɛbɛyɛ a ɛbɛyɛ deɛ ɛbɛyɛ (present simple → do/does; past simple → did; presente perfecto → have/has; modales → el mismo modal). Sɛ ɛyɛ mmerɛwa a ɛyɛ mmerɛwa a, yɛde 'so + ahyɛnsɛm + ɔmanfoɔ' (e.g., 'So do I'). Sɛ ɛyɛ mmerɛwa a ɛyɛ mmerɛwa a, yɛde 'neither/nor + ahyɛnsɛm + ɔmanfoɔ' (e.g., 'Neither have we'). Ɛne sɛnkyerɛnne nso wɔ 'do/does/did' mu nkyerɛkyerɛ a ɛyɛ ɛkwan a ɛfiri nea ɛwɔ hɔ (e.g., 'She speaks French better than I do'), ne 'so' ma ama yɛn kasa biara a ɛtɔ so ara (e.g., 'I think so'). Wɔ English a ɛyɛ ɛkwan a ɛfiri nea ɛwɔ hɔ mu, wɔntu 'also' anaa 'too' wɔ nkyerɛkyerɛ no mu; ɛsɛ yɛde ahyɛnsɛm. Nso, sɛ yɛde 'so' wɔ mmerɛwa a ɛyɛ mmerɛwa a, ahyɛnsɛm no bɛyɛ deɛ ɛbɛyɛ nea ɛbɛyɛ nea ɛbɛyɛ, ɛntumi nea ɛbɛyɛ nea ɛbɛyɛ.

examples.note: Wɔde 'have' efisɛ ɛyɛ present perfect. Ahyɛnsɛm no ne ɔmanfoɔ no yɛ ɛkwan a ɛfiri nea ɛwɔ hɔ.

examples.original: They will arrive early, and so will we.

examples.translation: Wɔbɛba paa, yɛn nso.
examples.note: Sɛ ɛyɛ modal a ɛne 'will' a, yɛde modal no ara wɔ mmerɛwa mu.

examples.original: She works hard, and so do I.

examples.note: Wɔ present simple mu, yɛde 'do' sɛ ɛyɛ I/you/we/they, nanso yɛde 'does' sɛ ɛyɛ he/she/it.

examples.original: We don't like spicy food, and neither does Mary.
examples.phonetic: /wi dəʊnt laɪk ˈspaɪsi fuːd ænd ˈnaɪðə dʌz ˈmeəri/
examples.translation: Yɛmpɛ spicy food, ne Mary nso.
examples.note: Sɛ mmerɛwa a ɛyɛ mmerɛwa a, yɛde 'neither' ne ahyɛnsɛm a ɛyɛ mmerɛwa a (ɛntumi mmerɛwa).

examples.original: I can't swim, and nor can my sister.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ kɑːnt swɪm ænd nɔː kən maɪ ˈsɪstə/
examples.translation: Mɛntumi swim, ne me sister nso.
examples.note: 'Nor' yɛ ɛkwan a ɛfiri nea ɛwɔ hɔ pɛ wɔ 'neither' ne yɛde modal no ara.

examples.original: They haven't finished, and neither has he.
examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ ˈhævənt ˈfɪnɪʃt ænd ˈnaɪðə hæz hiː/
examples.translation: Wɔammra no, ne he nso.
examples.note: Wɔ present perfect mu, yɛde 'has' sɛ ɛyɛ he/she/it ne 'have' sɛ ɛyɛ wɔn a wɔyɛ wɔn a wɔyɛ.

examples.original: She speaks French better than I do.
examples.phonetic: /ʃi spiːks frenʃ ˈbɛtə ðən aɪ duː/
examples.translation: She talk French pɛ wɔ me.
examples.note: 'Do' de 'speak' akɔ so ama yɛn kasa biara a ɛtɔ so ara.

examples.original: He didn't break the vase, but his brother did.
examples.phonetic: /hi ˈdɪdnt breɪk ðə vɑːz bʌt hɪz ˈbrʌðə dɪd/

examples.note: Wɔ past mu, yɛde 'did' de verb no akɔ so wɔ mmerɛwa a ɛyɛ mmerɛwa a.

examples.original: Do you think it will rain? - I think so.
examples.phonetic: /duː juː θɪŋk ɪt wɪl reɪn aɪ θɪŋk səʊ/
examples.translation: Wodii sɛ ɛbɛfa? - Ɛyɛ.
examples.note: 'So' de clause a ɛtɔ so ara ('it will rain') akɔ so wɔ mmerɛwa mu.

title: Advanced Discourse Markers for Cohesion / Nkyerɛntɔ́ asɛm a wɔde ma asɛm ka a wɔde ho nhwɛso
bridge: Wɔ Twi, nkyerɛntɔ́ asɛm a wɔde ma asɛm ka sɛ ‘nanso’, ‘na ɛno akyi’ ne ‘sɛe’ yɛ den sɛ wɔbɛka wɔn wɔ asɛm no mu paa ne wɔde wɔn kyerɛw wɔn a wɔde ho nhwɛso wɔ England kasa mu. Nanso, wɔ England kasa mu, pii wɔ nkyerɛntɔ́ asɛm no bɛtra wɔ asɛm no mu ansa na wɔde wɔn kyerɛw wɔn a wɔde ho nhwɛso, na ɛma ɛho nhwɛso ne ɛkyɛfa biara. Enti, pii wɔ nkyerɛntɔ́ asɛm a wɔde ho nhwɛso wɔ England kasa mu sɛ ‘though’ a wɔde wɔ asɛm no mu akɔso ntɛm nyɛ nkyerɛntɔ́ a ɛde ho nhwɛso wɔ Twi ne ɛbɛyɛ a wɔbɛtumi asɛm no. Fa akoma yɛ adanseɛ ne ɛkyɛfa a wɔde ho nhwɛso.
rule: Nkyerɛntɔ́ asɛm a wɔde ho nhwɛso wɔ England kasa mu (C1) ne: 1) Nkyerɛntɔ́ a wɔde kyerɛw ho nhwɛso: 'nevertheless', 'nonetheless', 'whereas', 'while', 'on the contrary', 'in contrast' (wɔde wɔn kyerɛw ho nhwɛso, na 'whereas' ne 'while' de wɔn kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso). 2) Nkyerɛntɔ́ a wɔde kyerɛw akɔsoa: 'consequently', 'therefore', 'thus', 'hence', 'accordingly', 'as a result' (wɔde wɔn kyerɛw akɔsoa; 'thus' ne 'hence' yɛ nkyerɛntɔ́ a wɔde ho nhwɛso wɔ akwan a wɔde wɔn kyerɛw din deɛ o, anaa wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso). 3) Nkyerɛntɔ́ a wɔde kyerɛw nkɔm: 'furthermore', 'moreover', 'in addition', 'besides' (wɔde wɔn kyerɛw nkɔm; 'besides' deɛ, wɔde no kyerɛw nkɔm wɔ asɛm a wɔde ho nhwɛso mu). 4) Nkyerɛntɔ́ a wɔde kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso: 'in other words', 'that is', 'namely', 'to put it differently' (wɔde wɔn kyerɛw anaa wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso). 5) Nkyerɛntɔ́ a wɔde kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso: 'for instance', 'for example', 'such as' (wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso). 6) Nkyerɛntɔ́ a wɔde kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso ne a wɔde kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso: 'incidentally', 'by the way', 'meanwhile', 'in the meantime' (wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso anaa a wɔde kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso). 7) Nkyerɛntɔ́ a wɔde kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso: 'admittedly', 'granted', 'even though' (wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso). 8) Nkyerɛntɔ́ a wɔde kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso: 'indeed', 'in fact', 'actually' (wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso). 9) Nkyerɛntɔ́ a wɔde kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso: 'in conclusion', 'to sum up', 'in summary', 'ultimately' (wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso). Wɔ asɛm no mu paa, wɔde wɔn kyerɛw adanseɛ; wɔ asɛm no mu ansa, wɔde wɔn kyerɛw adanseɛ; wɔ asɛm no mu akɔso, pii wɔ nkyerɛntɔ́ asɛm sɛ 'though' nni adanseɛ. Wɔ Twi, pii wɔ nkyerɛntɔ́ asɛm no de kyerɛw sɛ 'nanso', 'no obstante', 'además', 'por lo tanto', 'es decir', 'por ejemplo', etc., nanso asɛm no ne ɛkyɛfa a wɔde ho nhwɛso ne ɛbɛyɛ a wɔde wɔn kyerɛw wɔn a wɔde ho nhwɛso.

concept_examples.text: The project was challenging; nevertheless, the team managed to deliver it on time.
concept_examples.translation: Obiara pii a wɔyɛε no ho asɛm biara; nanso, ɛno ara na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈprɒdʒekt wɒz ˈtʃælɪndʒɪŋ; ˌnevəðəˈles, ðə tiːm ˈmænɪdʒd tə dɪˈlɪvər ɪt ɒn taɪm/

concept_examples.text: Whereas the previous report was optimistic, this one highlights several risks.
concept_examples.translation: Saa ɛbɛyɛ a, ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no, nanso ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /weərˈæz ðə ˈpriːviəs rɪˈpɔːt wɒz ˌɒptɪˈmɪstɪk, ðɪs wʌn ˈhaɪlaɪts ˈsevrəl rɪsks/

concept_examples.text: The company's profits have increased; consequently, they plan to expand.
concept_examples.translation: Ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no; na ɛno akyi, ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈkʌmpəniz ˈprɒfɪts hæv ɪnˈkriːst; ˈkɒnsɪkwəntli, ðeɪ plæn tə ɪkˈspænd/

concept_examples.text: He is an excellent candidate; indeed, his experience surpasses all others.
concept_examples.translation: Ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no; ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no, na ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /hiː ɪz ən ˈeksələnt kændɪdət; ɪnˈdiːd, hɪz ɪkˈspɪəriəns səˈpɑːsɪz ɔːl ˈʌðəz/

common_error.wrong: Although the weather was bad, but we went to the beach.
common_error.correct: Although the weather was bad, we went to the beach.
common_error.correct_alt: The weather was bad; nevertheless, we went to the beach.
common_error.explanation: Ɛyɛ den sɛ wɔbɛyɛ ɛyi wɔ Twi, efisɛ wɔde asɛm sɛ 'Although ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no, nanso wɔyɛε no' (ɛyɛ den sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no). Wɔ England kasa mu, ɛnyɛ den sɛ wɔbɛka 'although' ne 'but' kɔpem; na wɔde baako. Ma wɔde no kyerɛw, fa 'but' ho, na wɔde adanseɛ, anaa wɔde 'nevertheless' kyerɛw ne wɔde adanseɛ. Fa akoma sɛ 'although' de kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso, na asɛm no nni nkyerɛntɔ́ a ɛde ho nhwɛso.

levels.label: Contrast Markers
levels.translation: Nkyerɛntɔ́ a wɔde kyerɛw ho nhwɛso

examples.original: She is very introverted; however, she gives excellent presentations.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː ɪz ˈveri ˈɪntrəvɜːtɪd; haʊˈevə, ʃiː gɪvz ˈeksələnt ˌprezenˈteɪʃənz/
examples.translation: Ɛyɛ den sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no; nanso, ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no.
examples.note: 'However' de kyerɛw asɛm no mu ansa anaa ɛde kyerɛw asɛm no mu paa, na wɔde adanseɛ kyerɛw no. Wɔ Twi, 'nanso' de kyerɛw asɛm no mu ansa anaa ɛde kyerɛw asɛm no mu paa, nanso wɔde adanseɛ kyerɛw no pii.

examples.original: Unlike the North, the South of the country enjoys mild winters.
examples.phonetic: /ʌnˈlaɪk ðə nɔːθ, ðə saʊθ əv ðə ˈkʌntri ɪnˈdʒɔɪz maɪld ˈwɪntəz/
examples.translation: Saa ɛbɛyɛ a, ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no, na ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no.
examples.note: 'Unlike' yɛ nkyerɛntɔ́ a wɔde kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso, na ɛde kyerɛw 'a diferencia de'. Wɔ Twi, wɔde 'a diferencia de' + din kyerɛw, sɛ England kasa.

examples.original: He didn't fail the exam; on the contrary, he got the highest mark.
examples.phonetic: /hiː ˈdɪdnt feɪl ði ɪɡˈzæm; ɒn ðə ˈkɒntrəri, hiː gɒt ðə ˈhaɪɪst mɑːk/
examples.translation: Ɛnyɛ sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no; ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no, na ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no.
examples.note: 'On the contrary' de kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso ma wɔde no kyerɛw asɛm a ɛnyɛ den. Wɔ Twi, 'al contrario' de kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso, nanso pii wɔde 'por el contrario' kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso (ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no).

levels.label: Consequence and Addition Markers
levels.translation: Nkyerɛntɔ́ a wɔde kyerɛw akɔsoa ne nkɔm

examples.original: The new policy has reduced costs; therefore, the company can invest more in R&D.
examples.phonetic: /ðə njuː ˈpɒləsi hæz rɪˈdjuːst kɒsts; ˈðeəfɔː, ðə ˈkʌmpəni kæn ɪnˈvest mɔːr ɪn ɑːr ənd diː/
examples.translation: Wɔyɛε no ho asɛm biara; na ɛno akyi, ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no.
examples.note: 'Therefore' yɛ nkyerɛntɔ́ a wɔde ho nhwɛso wɔ asɛm a wɔde ho nhwɛso mu sɛ 'so'. Wɔ Twi, 'por lo tanto' yɛ nkyerɛntɔ́ a ɛde ho nhwɛso. Wɔde no kyerɛw asɛm no mu paa ne wɔde adanseɛ kyerɛw no, anaa wɔde no kyerɛw asɛm no mu ansa ne wɔde adanseɛ kyerɛw no.

examples.original: The results were inconclusive; hence, further research is needed.
examples.phonetic: /ðə rɪˈzʌlts wɜːr ˌɪnkənˈkluːsɪv; hens, ˈfɜːðə rɪˈsɜːtʃ ɪz ˈniːdɪd/
examples.translation: Wɔnyɛε no ho asɛm biara; ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no, na ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no.
examples.note: 'Hence' yɛ nkyerɛntɔ́ a wɔde ho nhwɛso wɔ akwan a wɔde wɔn kyerɛw din deɛ o, na wɔde no pii wɔ asɛm a wɔde ho nhwɛso mu. Wɔ Twi, 'de ahí que' de kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso (ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no). Fa akoma yɛ ɛkwan a wɔde kyerɛw asɛm no.

examples.original: Furthermore, the committee would like to thank the volunteers.
examples.phonetic: /ˈfɜːðəmɔː, ðə kəˈmɪti wʊd laɪk tə θæŋk ðə ˌvɒlənˈtɪəz/
examples.translation: Enti, ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no, na ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no.
examples.note: 'Furthermore' de kyerɛw nkɔm wɔ asɛm a wɔde ho nhwɛso mu. Wɔ Twi, 'además' yɛ nkyerɛntɔ́ a ɛde ho nhwɛso, na wɔde no wɔ asɛm biara mu.

levels.label: Reformulation and Exemplification
levels.translation: Nkyerɛntɔ́ a wɔde kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso ne a wɔde kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso

examples.original: The company is downsizing, in other words, it will lay off many employees.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈkʌmpəni ɪz ˈdaʊnsaɪzɪŋ, ɪn ˈʌðə wɜːdz, ɪt wɪl leɪ ɒf ˈmeni ɪmˈplɔɪiːz/
examples.translation: Wɔyɛε no ho asɛm biara, ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no, ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no.
examples.note: 'In other words' de kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso ne wɔde asɛm bi kyerɛw. Wɔ Twi, 'es decir' yɛ nkyerɛntɔ́ a ɛde ho nhwɛso pii, na 'o sea' yɛ nkyerɛntɔ́ a ɛde ho nhwɛso wɔ asɛm a ɛnyɛ den.

examples.original: Some participants, namely those with prior experience, found the task easy.
examples.phonetic: /sʌm pɑːˈtɪsɪpənts, ˈneɪmli ðəʊz wɪð ˈpraɪə ɪkˈspɪəriəns, faʊnd ðə tɑːsk ˈiːzi/
examples.translation: Pii wɔ nkyerɛntɔ́ asɛm no, ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no, na ɛno na ɛyɛε sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no.
examples.note: 'Namely' de kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso. Wɔ Twi, 'a saber' yɛ nkyerɛntɔ́ a ɛde ho nhwɛso wɔ akwan a wɔde wɔn kyerɛw din deɛ o, na wɔde no wɔ asɛm a wɔde ho nhwɛso mu; wɔde 'específicamente' kyerɛw.

examples.original: To illustrate, let's consider a real-world example.
examples.phonetic: /tə ˈɪləstreɪt, lets kənˈsɪdər ə rɪəl wɜːld ɪɡˈzɑːmpəl/
examples.translation: Ma wɔde asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso, yɛbɛka asɛm bi.
examples.note: 'To illustrate' de kyerɛw asɛm a ɛde ho nhwɛso. Wɔ Twi, 'para ilustrar' yɛ nkyerɛntɔ́ a ɛde ho nhwɛso wɔ asɛm a wɔde ho nhwɛso mu.

translations.tw: Nkyerɛntɔ́ asɛm a wɔde ma asɛm ka a wɔde ho nhwɛso

title: Hedging and Tentativeness / Matización ne mmara ne kyerɛw
bridge: Wɔ Twi, modality epistemic kyerɛw wɔ adwuma nnɛ ne nsɛm a ɛte sɛ 'sɛ ehu' anaa 'sɛ obi bɛka' ne subjunctive. Nso wɔ English, wɔde modal verbs (might, could), adverbs of doubt (perhaps, presumably), ne impersonal structures sɛ 'It is arguable that...' ma wɔn ani gu so ara. Abusua bi a ɛne ne sɛ wɔ English, wɔde mmara yi dii wɔ academic ne professional discourse, na wɔ Twi, obiara bɛka sɛ ɛyɛ paa. Enti, wɔ English, modifier no yɛɛ ɛbɛyɛ ne ɛbɛyɛ ne ɛbɛyɛ, na wɔ Twi, wɔde yɛɛ ɛbɛyɛ anaa ɛbɛyɛ.
rule:
Wɔ English, hedging yɛ:
- Modal verbs: may, might, could (possibility) ne should (weak probability).
- Adverbs ne expressions of doubt: perhaps, possibly, presumably, arguably, maybe.
- Verbs of opinion ne perception without commitment: I think, I believe, I suppose, I would say, I tend to think.
- Impersonal ne passive structures: It is often said that, It is widely believed that,
- Adjectives of doubt: possible, likely, unlikely, debatable, questionable.
- Use of past tense as a form of courtesy or hypothesis: Would you mind... I wondered...
- Wɔ C1, wɔde 'might' kyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ paa pɛ 'may'; 'could' de ma amo kyerɛw, ne 'should' de ma expectation. Modifier no yɛɛ ɛbɛyɛ ne ɛbɛyɛ ne ɛbɛyɛ: 'He could be lying' vs 'He might be lying' vs 'He could possibly be lying'.

concept_examples.text: It might be argued that the results are inconclusive.
concept_examples.translation: ɛbɛyɛ sɛ wɔde nsɛm no kyerɛ sɛ ɛnyɛ paa.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪt maɪt bi ˈɑːrɡjud ðæt ðə rɪˈzʌlts ɑːr ˌɪnkənˈkluːsɪv/

concept_examples.text: The findings presumably reflect a wider trend.
concept_examples.translation: Nsɛm no kyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ paa sɛ ɛyɛ nokware.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈfaɪndɪŋz prɪˈzuːməbli rɪˈflɛkt ə ˈwaɪdər trɛnd/

concept_examples.text: I would suggest that alternative explanations are possible.
concept_examples.translation: Mɛka sɛ ɛyɛ paa sɛ ɛyɛ nokware.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd səˈdʒɛst ðæt ɔːlˈtɜːrnətɪv ˌɛkspləˈneɪʃənz ɑːr ˈpɑːsəbəl/

common_error.wrong: Maybe the results are not conclusive.
common_error.correct: The results may not be conclusive.
common_error.correct_alt: It could be argued that the results are not conclusive.
common_error.explanation: Ɛyɛ sɛ obi bɛka 'maybe' (sɛ ehu) wɔ nsɛm no mu, na ɛyɛ nokware na ɛnyɛ formal ne ɛnyɛ precise. Wɔ academic anaa professional contexts, wɔpɛ sɛ wɔde modal verbs sɛ 'may' anaa 'might' anaa impersonal structures ma wɔn ani gu so ara. Enti, Twi speakers de 'maybe' kyerɛ 'sɛ ehu', na wɔ English, wɔde verb modal ma wɔn ani gu so ara. Ma wɔde yɛɛ ɛbɛyɛ, ɛsɛ sɛ woato alternative forms ne modifier no yɛɛ ɛbɛyɛ.

examples.original: She might have missed the train.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː maɪt hæv mɪst ðə treɪn/
examples.translation: Ɛbɛyɛ sɛ anka ɛno ara na ɛba.

title: Complex Verb Patterns: Double Objects / Nkyea a Wɔ Ewiase: Mmusuo Mmienu
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnka mmoa 'a' anaa 'para' ma ama no ho nhwea, na sɛnkyerɛnee no yɛ ɔyɛ. Wɔ English, nkyea a wɔ ewiase pii bu a wɔde mmusuo mmienu: 'give something to somebody' anaa 'give somebody something', nanso nyinaa a wɔ ewiase no remma mmusuo mmienu. Enti, wɔ English no, mmusuo a ɛnyɛ preposition no sɛ ɔbɛka akyi mmusuo a ɛyɛ direct no, na sɛ yɛde Hispanic akyi a, ɛno ara na ɛbɛba. Nokware bi nso: nkyea a wɔ ewiase 'explain' anaa 'suggest' no remma mmusuo mmienu ('explain me' yɛ ɔkwan foforo), nanso wɔ Twi no, 'explícame' yɛ ɔyɛ.
rule: Wɔ English no, nkyea a wɔ ewiase ditransitive no ne mmusuo mmienu: (1) nkyea + mmusuo a ɛyɛ indirect (person) + mmusuo a ɛyɛ direct (thing) — 'give John a book' — na (2) nkyea + mmusuo a ɛyɛ direct + 'to/for' + mmusuo a ɛyɛ indirect — 'give a book to John'. Nyinaa a wɔ ewiase no remma mmusuo mmienu. Nkyea a wɔ ewiase 'give', 'send', 'show', 'tell', 'teach', 'lend', 'pass', 'offer', 'owe', 'promise' no bu mmusuo mmienu. Nkyea a wɔ ewiase 'explain', 'describe', 'suggest', 'mention', 'announce', 'report', 'say', 'admit', 'confess' no remma mmusuo a ɛyɛ 'to' (remma mmusuo mmienu a ɛnyɛ preposition). Wɔ 'buy', 'get', 'make', 'cook', 'find', 'save' no, wɔde 'for' ma ama no ho nhwea (e.g., 'buy a gift for her' anaa 'buy her a gift'). Sɛ mmusuo a ɛyɛ direct no yɛ pronoun (it, them), ɛno ara na ɛbɛba sɛ wɔde prepositional construction no ma no: 'give it to me', ɛnyɛ 'give me it'. Nkyea bi nso wɔ a wɔhyia preposition foforo, sɛ 'provide somebody with something' anaa 'explain something to somebody'.

title: Nuances of Tense and Aspect / Mmra pɔ wɔ nkyea ne ahoɔden wɔ Adwene Kasa
bridge: Wɔ España kasa mu, ahoɔden a wɔabɔ wɔ ahoden a ɛyɛ perfective ne imperfective te sɛ wɔde wɔn kyerɛw wo a wɔde wɔn kyerɛw wo a wɔde wɔn kyerɛw wo (pretérito indefinido vs. imperfecto), na wɔ English mu, ahoɔden ka ho nhwɛso wɔde ahoden a ɛyɛ progressive ('-ing') ne perfect ('have + -ed') kyerɛw. Mmra bi a Espaniafoɔ rekɔ so wɔ English mu no, wɔde ahoden a ɛyɛ simple past kyerɛw asɛm a ɛyɛ wɔ awerɛho wɔ awerɛho a eku (ɛ. 'I worked' na ɛsɛ sɛ 'I was working') anaa wɔde ahoden a ɛyɛ present perfect (he comido) ne ahoden a ɛyɛ simple past (comí) kyerɛw wɔ English mu. Mmra bi aka ho nhwɛso no, English nni ahoden a ɛde 'pretérito pluscuamperfecto' a ɛde wɔ España kasa mu ma wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm a ɛfiri awerɛho, na wɔde ahoden a ɛyɛ past perfect ne ahoɔden a ɛde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm a ɛfiri awerɛho a wɔde wɔn kyerɛw wɔ España kasa mu.
rule: 1. **Progressive vs. Simple Aspect**: Wɔ English mu, wɔde ahoden a ɛyɛ present progressive (am/is/are + -ing) kyerɛw asɛm a ɛyɛ wɔ awerɛho wɔ awerɛho a eku, na wɔde ahoden a ɛyɛ present simple (base form, -s wɔ third person mu) kyerɛw mmara ne nnwimma a ɛyɛ den. Wɔ awerɛho a eku, 'was/were + -ing' de asɛm a ɛyɛ wɔ awerɛho wɔ awerɛho a eku kyerɛw, na wɔde ahoden a ɛyɛ simple past (verb in -ed anaa irregular) kyerɛw asɛm a ɛyɛ wɔ awerɛho anaa asɛm a ɛyɛ wɔ awerɛho a eku. 2. **Perfect Aspects**: 'Present perfect' (have/has + -ed) de asɛm a ɛfiri awerɛho ne awerɛho kyerɛw (asɛm a ɛyɛ anaa asɛm a ɛyɛ, na ɛnni awerɛho biara). 'Past perfect' (had + -ed) de asɛm a ɛfiri awerɛho a ɛfiri awerɛho biara kyerɛw. Wɔ España kasa mu, ahoden a ɛyɛ present perfect (he hecho) ne pluscuamperfecto (había hecho) yɛ den, nanso wɔn ho nhwɛso nni hɔ. 3. **Stative verbs** (like, know, believe, want): wɔn a wɔde wɔn kyerɛw wɔ ahoden a ɛyɛ progressive mu no, wɔde wɔn kyerɛw wɔ ahoden a ɛyɛ progressive mu; nanso, wɔde wɔn kyerɛw wɔ ahoden a ɛyɛ progressive mu (ɛ. 'be having' vs. 'have'). 4. **Expressing Future**: Wɔ English mu, wɔde ahoden a ɛyɛ present continuous (ma wɔn a wɔyɛ ho nhwɛso), 'be going to' (adwene), ne 'will' (adwene a ɛyɛ den, adwene). 5. **Aspect with 'used to' and 'would'**: Ma wɔn a wɔyɛ ho nhwɛso wɔ awerɛho, wɔde 'used to' (solía) anaa 'would' (solía) kyerɛw asɛm a ɛyɛ wɔ awerɛho a eku. 6. **Narration**: Wɔ adwene a ɛyɛ wɔ awerɛho a eku mu, wɔde ahoden a ɛyɛ simple past (asɛm a ɛyɛ den) ne ahoden a ɛyɛ past progressive (asɛm a ɛyɛ den) kyerɛw. Wɔde ahoden a ɛyɛ past perfect kyerɛw asɛm a ɛfiri awerɛho. Wɔn a wɔde wɔn kyerɛw wɔ España kasa mu no, wɔn ho nhwɛso nni hɔ.

title: Advanced Passives / Pasifa wɔ Twi
bridge: Wɔ Twi, nsɛmfuor a wɔde kyerɛ sɛ 'se koraa sɛ' anaa 'wɔte sɛ' yɛ mfatoho ma wɔbɛka adwene anaa nnwim a wɔnkyerɛkyerɛ no nni hɔ. Wɔ Gyeman ne Frɛnkye, nsɛmfuor no wɔde pasifa a wɔnkyerɛkyerɛ no nni hɔ kyerɛma: 'it is said that', 'it is believed that', anaa pasifa a wɔde to-infinitive kyerɛma 'is said to be'. Nnipa a wɔbɛka ho asɛm no, sɛnea wɔde verb kyerɛma wɔ Gyeman ne Frɛnkye no, no yɛ nneɛma a wɔn atɛnkyea. Ɛno nso, wɔ Twi, wɔnnsusuw verb no ne subject no ho nhia, na wɔ Gyeman ne Frɛnkye, wɔde 'there' kyerɛma wɔ pasifa a wɔde kyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ, na ɛno nni adwene wɔ Twi.
rule: Wɔ Gyeman ne Frɛnkye, wɔde pasifa wɔ kyerɛw a wɔde kyerɛ adwene, akwantu anaa nnwim a wɔnkyerɛkyerɛ no nni hɔ. Ɛyɛ den a wɔde kyerɛma: 1) Pasifa a wɔde subject kyerɛma: 'Subject + passive verb + to-infinitive' (mfatoho 'He is said to be very rich'). Subject a wɔde kyerɛma wɔ clause a ɛso no, ɛma ɛho adansɛn wɔ pasifa no mu, na verb a wɔde to-infinitive kyerɛma no, ɛne 'to be', 'to have been', anaa 'to be doing'. 2) Pasifa a wɔnkyerɛkyerɛ no nni hɔ: 'It + passive verb + that-clause' (mfatoho 'It is believed that the economy will improve'). Nsɛmfuor no te sɛ 'es/es creído que' wɔ Twi, nanso wɔ Gyeman ne Frɛnkye, ɛyɛ mfatoho paa. Ɛno nso, wɔde 'There + passive verb + to be' (mfatoho 'There is said to be a shortage of water') ma wɔde kyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ anaa ɛwɔ hɔ. De nsɛmfuor a ɛbɛyɛ a wɔde kyerɛma: pasifa a wɔde subject kyerɛma no yɛ formal paa na wɔde no wɔ akwantu a wɔde kyerɛma wɔ Gyeman ne Frɛnkye. Ka sɛ wɔde 'report', 'say', 'believe', 'think', 'know', 'expect', 'allege', 'claim', 'consider' kyerɛma wɔ nsɛmfuor no mu. Wɔ verb bi a wɔde kyerɛma sɛ 'suggest', 'propose', wɔde pasifa a wɔnkyerɛkyerɛ no nni hɔ kyerɛma.

concept_examples.text: It is believed that the company will announce new plans soon.
concept_examples.translation: Wɔte sɛ ɔman no bɛkae nnipa pii wɔ ɔkwan a ɛbɛn ka.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪt ɪz bɪˈliːvd ðæt ðə ˈkʌmpəni wɪl əˈnaʊns nuː plænz suːn/

concept_examples.text: The suspect is alleged to have stolen the money.
concept_examples.translation: Se koraa sɛ ɔha no dee adwuma no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈsʌspekt ɪz əˈlɛdʒd tə hæv ˈstoʊlən ðə ˈmʌni/

concept_examples.text: There is said to be a hidden treasure in the old castle.
concept_examples.translation: Wɔkae sɛ ɛyɛ sika paa wɔ ɔkɔtɔ a ɛyɛ ɔkɔtɔ no mu.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðɛr ɪz sɛd tə bi ə ˈhɪdən ˈtrɛʒər ɪn ði oʊld ˈkæsəl/

concept_examples.text: The new policy is expected to reduce costs significantly.
concept_examples.translation: Wɔhwɛ sɛ mmara pono no bɛto so ma ɛto so.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðə nuː ˈpɑləsi ɪz ɪkˈspɛktɪd tə rɪˈdus kɔsts sɪɡˈnɪfɪkəntli/

common_error.wrong: It is said that there is a problem with the system.
common_error.correct: There is said to be a problem with the system.
common_error.correct_alt: It is said that the system has a problem.
common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi, wɔde 'it is said that' ne 'there is' kyerɛma, na ɛno ma ɛyɛ nsɛm a ɛnni adwene. Wɔ Gyeman ne Frɛnkye, sɛ wopɛ sɛ wode kyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ, de 'there + passive + to be' kyerɛma. Anaa, wɔde nsɛm no susuw no kyerɛma.

levels.label: Impersonal Passive with 'It'
levels.translation: Pasifa a wɔnkyerɛkyerɛ no nni hɔ ne 'It'

examples.original: It is estimated that over a million people visit the site each year.
examples.phonetic: /ɪt ɪz ˈɛstəmeɪtɪd ðæt ˈoʊvər ə ˈmɪljən ˈpiːpəl ˈvɪzɪt ðə saɪt iːtʃ jɪr/
examples.translation: Wɔte sɛ nnipa pii rekɔ ɛkɔntɔ no biara.
examples.note: De 'it' + passive verb (sɛ 'estimated', 'believed', 'said') + clause a wɔde 'that' kyerɛma ma wode kyerɛ adwene anaa akwantu.

examples.original: It is thought that the election results will be close.
examples.phonetic: /ɪt ɪz θɔt ðæt ði ɪˈlɛkʃən rɪˈzʌlts wɪl bi kloʊs/
examples.translation: Wɔhwehwɛ sɛ nnipa bɛkɔ so wɔ ɔkwan a ɛbɛn ka.
examples.note: Wɔ Twi, 'se koraa sɛ' yɛ mfatoho paa wɔ Gyeman ne Frɛnkye; wɔ Gyeman ne Frɛnkye, de pasifa a wɔnkyerɛkyerɛ no nni hɔ ma ɛho adansɛn yɛ formal.

examples.original: It has been reported that the company is planning to expand.
examples.phonetic: /ɪt hæz bɪn rɪˈpɔrtɪd ðæt ðə ˈkʌmpəni ɪz ˈplænɪŋ tə ɪkˈspænd/
examples.translation: Wɔaka sɛ ɔman no rekɔ so wɔ ɔkwan a ɛbɛn ka.
examples.note: De perfect passive tense ('has been reported') kyerɛma ma wode kyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ wɔ ɔkwan a ɛda no.

levels.label: Personal Passive with Infinitive
levels.translation: Pasifa a wɔde subject kyerɛma ne infinitive

examples.original: The mayor is considered to be the most influential person in the city.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈmeɪər ɪz kənˈsɪdərd tə bi ðə moʊst ˌɪnfluˈɛnʃəl ˈpɜrsən ɪn ðə ˈsɪti/
examples.translation: Wɔhwehwɛ sɛ ɔman no yɛ ɔha a ɔwɔ hɔ.
examples.note: De 'consider' kyerɛma, de 'to be' kyerɛma ne noun anaa adjective.

examples.original: The ancient building is said to have been built in the 12th century.
examples.phonetic: /ði ˈeɪnʃənt ˈbɪldɪŋ ɪz sɛd tə hæv bɪn bɪlt ɪn ðə twɛlfθ ˈsɛnʧəri/
examples.translation: Wɔkae sɛ ɛkɔntɔ no yɛe wɔ ɔkɔtɔ a ɛyɛ ɔkɔtɔ no mu.
examples.note: De past actions kyerɛma, de 'to have been + past participle' kyerɛma.

examples.original: The children are believed to be hiding in the forest.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈʧɪldrən ɑr bɪˈliːvd tə bi ˈhaɪdɪŋ ɪn ðə ˈfɔrɪst/
examples.translation: Wɔte sɛ mmofra no rekɔ wɔ asɔre no mu.
examples.note: De ongoing actions kyerɛma, de 'to be + gerund' (continuous form) kyerɛma.

levels.label: Passive with 'There' and Other Variations
levels.translation: Pasifa ne 'There' ne nsɛmfuor bi wɔn a wɔde kyerɛma

examples.original: There are thought to be serious problems with the current system.
examples.phonetic: /ðɛr ɑr θɔt tə bi ˈsɪriəs ˈprɑbləmz wɪð ðə ˈkɜrənt ˈsɪstəm/
examples.translation: Wɔhwehwɛ sɛ ɛyɛ nnipa pii wɔ ɔkwan a ɛbɛn ka.
examples.note: De 'There are thought to be' kyerɛma ma wode kyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ nnipa pii.

examples.original: The new law is claimed to have reduced crime by 30%.
examples.phonetic: /ðə nuː lɔ ɪz kleɪmd tə hæv rɪˈdust kraɪm baɪ ˈθɜrti pərˈsɛnt/
examples.translation: Wɔaka sɛ mmara pono no ahyɛ wɔ ɔkwan a ɛbɛn ka.
examples.note: Wɔde verb sɛ 'claim', 'allege', 'report' kyerɛma wɔ nsɛmfuor no mu.

examples.original: He is known to have worked for the government in the past.
examples.phonetic: /hi ɪz noʊn tə hæv wɜrkt fər ðə ˈgʌvərnmənt ɪn ðə pæst/
examples.translation: Wɔte sɛ ɔno na ɔdeɛ no wɔ hɔ.
examples.note: De 'known' kyerɛma, de 'to have + past participle' kyerɛma de past actions kyerɛma.
